mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-0 collapse in WORKPLACES signals reduced commuter foot traffic, which lowers nearby retail visits with a lag. If WORKPLACES remains depressed, RETAIL_REC should fall further over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -16.3 to -44.3 in week-0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the prior 28 days while WORKPLACES stays at or below the week-0 level.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated, people substitute home-centered activity for discretionary shopping trips, so retail visits decline within one to two weeks. The week-0 rise in RESIDENTIAL should therefore precede lower RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 13 points while WORKPLACES remains below -20 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 13 while WORKPLACES remains below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES raises in-person trip chaining, which increases retail-and-recreation demand with about a one-month lag. If both series improve together, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both below baseline but moved unevenly in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days despite a joint upward move in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden worsening in TRANSIT below -25 points marks renewed access frictions or service cutbacks, which directly suppress discretionary shopping visits within one week. RETAIL_REC should weaken immediately after such a transit break.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 points after being above -22 points the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -20.6 in week-1 to -26.0 in week-0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after TRANSIT crosses below -25 from a higher prior reading.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM alongside stable or improving PARKS indicates weekend errand and outdoor trip substitution that competes with retail browsing. Over the next two weeks, that mix should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near +30 and PARKS improved to -19.6 in week-0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated and PARKS does not weaken.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS rebound while RETAIL_REC is still depressed, leisure demand is being diverted outdoors rather than into stores. That diversion should keep retail mobility flat-to-lower over the next four weeks unless WORKPLACES also recover materially.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -20 points while RETAIL_REC remains below -25 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -26.4 to -19.6 while RETAIL_REC stayed negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying above -20 and WORKPLACES not recovering.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week drop in GROCERY_PHARM after a prior rise signals tighter crowd management or fewer essential trips, which often spills over into lower discretionary shopping within two weeks. If GROCERY_PHARM rolls over, RETAIL_REC should follow downward.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by at least 3 points after being above 30 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM peaked at 31.0 in week-1 and eased to 30.0 in week-0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM falls from above 30 by at least 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains deeply negative while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, daytime activity stays anchored at home and retail trips do not recover. This joint pattern should keep RETAIL_REC below the last-four-week mean over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -44.3 and RESIDENTIAL rose to 14.3 in week-0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES stays very low and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated.
